- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% below peak or use 3-period moving average.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3) and prices are falling, model frequently underestimates; add 3–7% to forecast to account for mean reversion.  
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive; apply 5–10% downward bias for first 5–7 days.  
- If recent history shows strong downward trend (e.g., 3 consecutive drops >2%), model often fails to recognize continuation; apply 10–15% downward adjustment for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is mixed (0.0–0.5), model tends to be overly optimistic; use 5–10% downward correction for 3–7 day horizon.
